items.t: The District's Official Community Plan, Bylaw 7900, covers this area. Exact boundary streets are not verified; the confirmed anchors are Capilano Road itself, Capilano Suspension Bridge Park at 3735 Capilano Road, and the Cleveland Dam at the corridor's north end.

Naming split a buyer will meet: District and school sources use "Upper Capilano" for the plateau north of Highway 1 (Canyon Heights, Capilano Highlands, Grousewoods) and "Lower Capilano / Lions Gate" for the Marine Drive end south of the highway.

Condo stock on the corridor is scarce and scattered: the one verified apartment building in sits on Capilano Road itself in the corridor's mid-section, near the Edgemont Village side. The rest of the corridor is detached houses under the District's R1 and R2 zones.

Main streets and transit: Capilano Road is the spine — south to Marine Drive and the Lions Gate Bridge, north to the Cleveland Dam and Grouse Mountain (6400 Nancy Greene Way, reached only by Capilano Road). TransLink route 236 runs on Capilano Road the length of the corridor toward Grouse Mountain and Lonsdale Quay; route 246 crosses the corridor via Capilano Road and Montroyal Boulevard with downtown trips over the Lions Gate Bridge.

Nearby areas: Canyon Heights and Edgemont Village (east), Capilano Highlands and Grousewoods (north), Norgate and Pemberton Heights in the lowlands (south-east, below Highway 1), and — across the Capilano River — West Vancouver's Park Royal / Ambleside side. Edgemont is one of the District OCP's six Village Centres and is the corridor's walk-to/drive-to retail; no shopping centre or grocery store on the Capilano Road corridor itself is confirmed.

blocks.text: Local rules that affect condo buyers in Capilano

items.t: District of North Vancouver tax timing: District 2026 property taxes were due July 2, 2026, with a 5% penalty after July 2, 2026 and a further 5% after September 1, 2026; the 2026 residential municipal rate is 1.83419 and the total residential rate is 3.28195 per $1,000 of assessed value. District single-family utility fees in 2026 include water at $932.80 and sewer/drainage at $1,255.60, with combined single-family utilities of $2,571.20.

The dam above the corridor is a 1954 drinking-water dam. The Cleveland Dam at the head of Capilano River Regional Park was completed in 1954 and stands 91 m high, holding back Capilano Lake, the drinking-water reservoir above the corridor; Fisheries and Oceans Canada's Capilano River Hatchery below the dam was completed in 1971 and normally draws about 250,000 visitors a year.

The school with the area's name is not in the area. Capilano Elementary, 1230 West 20th Street, carries the Capilano name but sits in the City of North Vancouver lowlands south of the corridor — marketing it as this area's school without an address-level catchment check would be wrong.

The library with the area's name is in Edgemont Village. The Capilano Library, 3045 Highland Boulevard, is described by the North Vancouver District Public Library as "located in the heart of Edgemont Village," east of the corridor — the corridor's services cluster in the neighbouring village centre, not on Capilano Road.

A detached lot here can already hold three homes' worth of occupants. Since June 2024, a principal dwelling plus a secondary suite plus a coach house — three units total — are permitted on single-family zoned properties within the Urban Containment Boundary, and the District's SSMUH classification can potentially allow up to 6 units on non-exempt lots over 280 m² within 400 m of a frequent-transit bus stop. That infill potential, not strata product, is the corridor's density story.

The flood data is modelled to 2100. The District publishes property-level GeoWeb reports including modelled flood construction levels for a 2100 (2080s) horizon plus 0.6 m — a canyon-edge buyer's renovation budget should be priced against that horizon, not against today's water levels.

blocks.text: Local rules that affect townhome buyers in Capilano

items.t: Form B diligence (Canyon Park and any strata purchase compared nearby): Strata Property Act s. 59 — the Form B states the lot's monthly strata fees, amounts owing, approved special levies still payable, the CRF balance and an insurance summary, with the rules, current budget, any Rental Disclosure Statement and the most recent depreciation report attached; provided within 7 days, maximum $35 plus up to 25 cents per page. Listing-level rental/pet lines are listing data, not bylaws — the Form B and registered bylaws govern.

District zoning and plan: the District of North Vancouver's Official Community Plan is Bylaw 7900 and its Zoning Bylaw is 3210 (the City of North Vancouver's OCP 8400 / Zoning 6700 pair does not apply on this corridor). Zoning Bylaw 3210, Section 525 (Bylaw 8799): the R1 zone minimum lot is 4,000 m² with 30 m width and 34 m depth, and the R2 zone minimum lot is 660 m² with 18 m width and 34 m depth, with modifiers R2(S1) at 335 m² / 10 m, R2(S2) at 1,100 m² / 24 m and R2(S3) at 4,000 m² / 30 m; an R2 principal building may include a secondary suite, and a coach house is a dwelling unit accessory to and detached from the principal dwelling unit.

Hazard permit areas: District OCP Bylaw 7900, Schedule B sets seven Development Permit Areas, including Protection of the Natural Environment, Streamside Protection, Wildfire Hazard, Creek Hazard and Slope Hazard — canyon-edge and ravine lots on this corridor are exactly the lots these areas were written for. The District publishes property-level GeoWeb reports, including modelled flood construction levels for a 2100 (2080s) horizon plus 0.6 m.

The school and the library with the area's name are both somewhere else. Capilano Elementary (1230 West 20th Street) sits in the City lowlands south of the corridor, and the Capilano Library (3045 Highland Boulevard) is described by the North Vancouver District Public Library as "located in the heart of Edgemont Village," east of the corridor — the corridor's services cluster in the neighbouring village centre, not on Capilano Road. The nearest full-service recreation centre is the Delbrook Community Recreation Centre, 851 West Queens Road.

The District is the big municipality, not the small one. The District of North Vancouver's 2021 Census population was 88,168, in 32,700 of 34,179 total private dwellings on 160.66 km² (Statistics Canada, 2021 Census Profile) — the corridor's rural-canyon feel sits inside a large urban district, which is why its permit areas, not a village plan, govern the lots.

items.t: Established-street house lots: The canyon and plateau streets are historic subdivision fabric — built lots, not a lot offering.

Lot character, as the bylaw states it: R1 minimum lot 4,000 m² with 30 m width and 34 m depth; R2 minimum lot 660 m² with 18 m width and 34 m depth; modifiers R2(S1) at 335 m² / 10 m, R2(S2) at 1,100 m² / 24 m and R2(S3) at 4,000 m² / 30 m. Zone minimums only — not a claim about any existing lot's size; the zone on a single lot is confirmed through the District's GeoWeb.

Serviced position, as the District states it: District single-family utility fees in 2026 include water at $932.80 and sewer/drainage at $1,255.60, with combined single-family utilities of $2,571.20 — the corridor's established lots sit inside that District system on the District's wording. Parcel-level septic or well status: Not verified; confirm the specific parcel with the District.

ALR vs non-ALR: no ALR parcel on the corridor is documented; parcel-level ALR status is listed not verified there. No ALR percentage split is stated — check any specific parcel on Agricultural Land Commission mapping. The canyon and reservoir lands above the corridor are regional park and drinking-water reservoir (Capilano Lake behind the Cleveland Dam) — protected/watershed land, not buildable lot area.

Flood/hazard position: the District publishes property-level GeoWeb reports, including modelled flood construction levels for a 2100 (2080s) horizon plus 0.6 m — a per-parcel check, not a corridor-wide designation asserted here.

No bare-land strata plan on the Capilano Road corridor was verified: If a corridor listing ever shows a strata plan number on a house lot, treat it as not confirmed until title and the strata plan are pulled — the BC strata diligence block in states what would then apply.

items.t: Nearby areas: Canyon Heights and Edgemont Village (east, across the Mosquito/Mackay creek ravines), Capilano Highlands and Grousewoods (north), Norgate and Pemberton Heights in the lowlands (south-east, below Highway 1), and — across the Capilano River — West Vancouver's Park Royal / Ambleside side.

Roads and transit: Capilano Road is the spine — south to Marine Drive and the Lions Gate Bridge, north to the Cleveland Dam and Grouse Mountain (6400 Nancy Greene Way; Capilano Road is the only road up to it) — and the Highway 1 interchange at Capilano Road is the corridor's highway access. Route 236 runs on Capilano Road the length of the corridor toward Grouse Mountain and Lonsdale Quay; route 232 runs via Capilano Road at the east side; route 246 crosses via Capilano Road and Montroyal Boulevard with downtown trips over the Lions Gate Bridge. Commute times in minutes: Not verified.

Anchors: Capilano River Regional Park (Metro Vancouver) runs along the river through and above the corridor (Capilano Pacific Trail, Coho Loop Trail); the Cleveland Dam (completed 1954, 91 m high) holds back Capilano Lake above the corridor; the Capilano River Hatchery (completed 1971) normally draws about 250,000 visitors a year. The Capilano Library, 3045 Highland Boulevard, sits in Edgemont Village east of the corridor; Delbrook Community Recreation Centre is at 851 West Queens Road. No shopping centre or grocery store on the corridor itself is confirmed — not verified; Edgemont is one of the District OCP's six Village Centres and is the corridor's retail. Nearest hospital: Lions Gate Hospital, 231 East 15th Street, North Vancouver.

blocks.text: Local rules that affect land buyers in Capilano

items.t: Zoning — District of North Vancouver Zoning Bylaw 3210 ONLY: Section 525 (Bylaw 8799) detached zones as stated in. The CITY of North Vancouver's Zoning Bylaw 6700 never applies to this District corridor.

OCP — District of North Vancouver Official Community Plan, Bylaw 7900: covers this area, including its Development Permit Areas in Schedule B; a Capilano-corridor-specific plan is not verified (none confirmed). The City's OCP Bylaw 8400 never applies here.

Added units / SSMUH, as the District and Province state them: since June 2024, District zoning permits a principal dwelling, a secondary suite and a coach house — three units total — on all single-family zoned properties within the Urban Containment Boundary. The District's GeoWeb SSMUH classification shows non-exempt lots potentially allowing up to 3 units at 280 m² or less, up to 4 units above 280 m², and up to 6 units above 280 m² within 400 m of a frequent-transit bus stop; provincial rules set 3 units on lots of 280 m² or smaller, 4 units on larger lots, and 6 units on larger lots within 400 m of a prescribed bus stop. Eligibility is parcel-specific — read the lot's GeoWeb SSMUH classification before pricing density in.

Hazard Development Permit Areas (OCP Bylaw 7900, Schedule B): seven Development Permit Areas, including Protection of the Natural Environment, Streamside Protection, Wildfire Hazard, Creek Hazard and Slope Hazard — canyon-edge and ravine lots on this corridor are exactly the lots these areas were written for. Whether a lot is in one is a District GeoWeb map check.

Reservoir context — diligence item: homes below the Cleveland Dam sit downstream of Capilano Lake, the drinking-water reservoir — confirm the parcel's hazard and insurance picture from the District GeoWeb reports rather than assuming from the street.

District property taxes and utilities: District of North Vancouver 2026 property taxes were due July 2, 2026, with a 5% penalty after July 2, 2026 and a further 5% after September 1, 2026; the 2026 residential municipal rate is 1.83419 and the total residential rate is 3.28195 per $1,000 of assessed value.

The dam above the corridor is a 1954 drinking-water work (2026-11-01 research): the Cleveland Dam stands 91 m high and holds back Capilano Lake — upper-corridor lots sit downstream of a reservoir, which is why the District's per-parcel GeoWeb hazard reports, not street reputation, settle the insurance and permit picture.

The hatchery is a working federal facility, not just a trail stop: Fisheries and Oceans Canada's Capilano River Hatchery (completed 1971) normally draws about 250,000 visitors a year for the coho and chinook runs — visitor traffic on the corridor is year-round, not only ski and bridge season.

Three units have been legal on these lots since June 2024: principal + secondary suite + coach house on single-family lots within the Urban Containment Boundary — the corridor's real density story is infill on existing lots, not new subdivisions.
